units.source_text: Properties of morphisms local in the fppf topology on the source

<STRUCT_0001>
Here are some properties of morphisms that are fppf local on the source.

The property <MATH_0001>``<MATH_0002> is locally of finite presentation''
is fppf local on the source.

Being locally of finite presentation is Zariski local on the source
and the target, see Morphisms,
Lemma <REF_0001>.
It is a property which is preserved under composition, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0002>.
This proves
(1), (2) and (3) of Lemma <REF_0003>.
The final condition (4) is
Lemma <REF_0004>. Hence we win.

The property <MATH_0001>``<MATH_0002> is locally of finite type''
is fppf local on the source.

Being locally of finite type is Zariski local on the source
and the target, see Morphisms,
Lemma <REF_0001>.
It is a property which is preserved under composition, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0002>, and
a flat morphism locally of finite presentation is locally of finite type, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0003>.
This proves
(1), (2) and (3) of Lemma <REF_0004>.
The final condition (4) is
Lemma <REF_0005>. Hence we win.

The property <MATH_0001>``<MATH_0002> is open''
is fppf local on the source.

Being an open morphism is clearly Zariski local on the source and the target.
It is a property which is preserved under composition, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0001>, and
a flat morphism of finite presentation is open, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0002>
This proves
(1), (2) and (3) of Lemma <REF_0003>.
The final condition (4) follows from
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0004>.
Hence we win.

The property <MATH_0001>``<MATH_0002> is universally open''
is fppf local on the source.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes.
Let <MATH_0002> be an fppf covering.
Denote <MATH_0003> the compositions.
We have to show that <MATH_0004> is universally open if and only if
each <MATH_0005> is universally open. If <MATH_0006> is universally open,
then also each <MATH_0007> is universally open since the maps
<MATH_0008> are universally open and compositions
of universally open morphisms are universally open
(Morphisms, Lemmas <REF_0001>
and <REF_0002>).
Conversely, assume each <MATH_0009> is universally open.
Let <MATH_0010> be a morphism of schemes.
Denote <MATH_0011> and <MATH_0012>.
Note that <MATH_0013> is an fppf covering also.
The morphisms <MATH_0014> are open by assumption.
Hence by the Lemma <REF_0003>
above we conclude that <MATH_0015> is open as desired.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\{X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ be an fppf covering.
Denote $f_i : X_i \to X$ the compositions.

each $f_i$ is universally open. If $f$ is universally open,
then also each $f_i$ is universally open since the maps
$X_i \to X$ are universally open and compositions
of universally open morphisms are universally open
(Morphisms, Lemmas \ref{morphisms-lemma-fppf-open}
and \ref{morphisms-lemma-composition-open}).
Conversely, assume each $f_i$ is universally open.
Let $Y' \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.

Note that $\{X_i' \to X'\}_{i \in I}$ is an fppf covering also.
The morphisms $f'_i : X_i' \to Y'$ are open by assumption.
Hence by the Lemma \ref{lemma-open-fppf-local-source}
above we conclude that $f' : X' \to Y'$ is open as desired.
\end{proof}
